study_identification.title: Individual-level deviations from normative brain morphology in violence, psychosis, and psychopathy

study_characteristics.study_objective: Assess individual-level deviations from normative brain morphology across schizophrenia spectrum disorder participants with and without a history of severe violence and violent participants without SSD, and test associations with psychopathy traits (PCL-R).

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Between-group comparisons on deviation scores using PALM GLM with 10,000 permutations, controlling for age (and ICV for volumes/areas), FWE-corrected across ROIs, contrasts, and modalities; age and site matched via MatchIt (1:1). Associations of deviation scores with PCL-R total tested in violent cohorts; no significant associations reported.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Individual-level deviation patterns were heterogeneous. All clinical groups showed more extreme negative deviations than controls (especially in SSD-V occipito-temporal/cerebellar regions), while positive deviations were fewer overall; no significant associations with psychopathy (PCL-R).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: SSD-V, SSD-NV, and nonSSD-V exhibited higher frequencies of extreme negative deviations than HC in cortical area and subcortical volume, but not thickness. For SSD-V, highest negative deviations occurred in collateral transverse sulcus (13.2%), lingual gyrus (10.5%), and cerebellar cortex volume (10.5%). SSD-NV showed occipital and suborbital sulcus involvement (~7.2%); nonSSD-V showed paracentral lobule/sulcus and middle frontal gyrus (20%/15%). Significant differences included SSD-V > HC for negative deviations in right subcallosal area (pmc-fwe = 0.020, t = 4.5, d = 1.17) and left medial occipito-temporal/lingual sulcus thickness (pc-fwe = 0.022, t = 4.3, d = 0.99). SSD-NV showed larger positive deviations in left inferior lateral ventricle and pallidum volumes vs HC. No significant associations were found between deviation scores and PCL-R total across violent participants.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Relatively small violent subgroup and male-only sample limit generalizability; ROI-level parcellation may underperform vs vertex-wise analyses; lack of adjustment for substance use and cumulative antipsychotic exposure; participation constraints for most severe cases; binary violence definition narrower than WHO; cross-sectional design limits causal inference; cross-sectional NM has lower individual-level prediction than longitudinal models.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Normative models: BrainCharts pretrained wBLR (sinh-arcsinh), PCNtoolkit v0.20 in Python 3.8; scanner included as predictor with adaptation via 998 local HCs for unseen scanners. Deviation analyses used PALM with rigorous multi-level FWE and site/age matching via MatchIt.
